### Management to Host Conference Call Monday at 5:00 p.m. ET


DURANGO, Colo., Oct. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rocky Mountain Chocolate Factory, Inc. (Nasdaq: RMCF) (the “Company” or “RMCF”), America’s Chocolatier® since 1981, is reporting financial and operating results for its second quarter of fiscal 2027, which ended August 31, 2026.


"Since stepping into the Interim CEO role, I have been encouraged by the way our leadership team has come together around a shared set of priorities for the business," said Allen Harper, Interim CEO. "With COO David Denker leading our day-to-day operations, our teams are increasingly aligned across the business. That alignment is strengthening accountability and decision-making as we build a stronger organization and position Rocky Mountain Chocolate Factory for sustainable growth and long-term shareholder value."


David Denker, Chief Operating Officer, added, "During the second quarter, we made progress improving production and execution across the business. August was our highest production and shipping month of the calendar year. Increasing production volume from our Durango facility remains a key priority as we prepare for the holiday season. Enhancements to our reporting platform, combined with our ERP capabilities, are providing our teams with greater visibility into demand, inventory and production requirements. These operational improvements, together with our continued focus on production efficiency and execution, contributed to the recovery in gross margin during the quarter. We believe there is additional opportunity to build on this progress as we move through the holiday season.”


Mr. Denker continued, “The acquisition of Chino Hills in July 2026 expanded our company-owned store base to five locations, while new franchised stores opened in Folsom, California, and Tinton Falls, New Jersey. As we grow our footprint and continue to enhance operations, we remain focused on consistent execution, supporting our franchisees and preserving the product quality and longstanding recipes that distinguish Rocky Mountain Chocolate Factory.”


**Fiscal Second Quarter 2027 Financial Results vs. Fiscal Second Quarter 2026**


- Total revenue was $6.7 million for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 compared to $6.8 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2026. Primarily due to lower Durango product sales and royalty and marketing fees which offset the increase in retail sales, driven by the larger company-owned store base and price increases.
- Total product and retail gross profit increased to $0.4 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 compared to a gross loss of less than $0.1 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2026. Gross margin improved to 8.0% from (0.6)%, reflecting pricing actions and production efficiencies.
- Total costs and expenses were $7.7 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, up from $7.3 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2026. The increase primarily reflects the larger company-owned store base and higher franchise and general and administrative costs. These increases were partially offset by lower cost of sales and sales and marketing expenses.
- Net loss was $1.3 million or $(0.14) per share for the second quarter of fiscal 2027, compared to a net loss of $0.7 million or $(0.09) per share in the second quarter of fiscal 2026.
- EBITDA loss was $0.7 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 compared to a loss of $0.1 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2026.


In the fiscal second quarter, the Board formed a strategic committee, which with the assistance of its advisors, is exploring strategic alternatives that may be available to the Company. Alternatives may include, among other things, a possible sale, merger, or other business combination, or a going-private transaction. In connection with this process, the Company has received expressions of interest from third parties. There can be no assurance that this review of strategic alternatives will result in any transaction or other strategic change.


**Subsequent Events**


Subsequent to quarter end, the Company completed a $6.6 million sale-leaseback transaction with American Heritage Legacies, LLC for its manufacturing facility located in Durango, Colorado. The sale was completed and the lease commenced on October 16, 2026. Net proceeds from the sale of the property have been used to repay $6.6 million in debt, which bears interest at 12% per annum. In connection with the repayment, the Company incurred prepayment penalties and related costs of $0.3 million.


On October 16, 2026, the Company entered into a loan agreement with Alpine Bank, where the Company received an advance of $2.0 million for working capital purposes. The loan matures on October 16, 2028, and bears interest at the prime rate plus 1%. Additional information is included in the Company’s Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended August 31, 2026.

**About Rocky Mountain Chocolate Factory, Inc.**


Rocky Mountain Chocolate Factory, Inc. is a leading franchisor, manufacturer and retailer of premium chocolates and other confectionery products. As America’s Chocolatier® since 1981, the Company produces an extensive assortment of premium chocolates, gourmet caramel apples and other handcrafted confections. Headquartered in Durango, Colorado, Rocky Mountain Chocolate Factory is ranked among Entrepreneur’s Franchise 500® for 2026. Together with its franchisees and licensees, the Company operates approximately 250 Rocky Mountain Chocolate Factory locations across the United States and internationally. The Company’s common stock is listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol “RMCF.”

**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


This press release includes non-GAAP financial measures, EBITDA loss and Adjusted Gross Margin. The Company defines EBITDA loss as net earnings before interest, taxes on income, and depreciation and amortization. The Company defines Adjusted Gross Margin as gross margin plus depreciation and amortization included in the cost of sales. Reconciliations of EBITDA loss and Adjusted Gross Margin with their most directly comparable GAAP measure is included in this press release.


These are supplemental measures of performance that are not required by, or presented in accordance with, GAAP. The Company believes Adjusted Gross Margin is useful to investors, as a supplement to gross margin and other performance measures calculated in accordance with GAAP, because it provides a measure of operating performance that is unaffected by non-cash depreciation and amortization. Management also uses Adjusted Gross Margin, rather than gross margin, to make incremental pricing decisions. The Company believes EBITDA (loss) is useful to investors because it helps them evaluate the Company's core operating performance without the effects of financing decisions, income taxes and non-cash depreciation and amortization, and management uses EBITDA (loss) to evaluate the Company's operating performance from period to period.


EBITDA (loss) and Adjusted Gross Margin have limitations as analytical tools because they exclude the impact of depreciation and amortization expense and, in the case of EBITDA (loss), interest and income taxes. They should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for any measure reported under GAAP. The Company's use of capital assets makes depreciation and amortization expense a necessary element of its costs and its ability to generate income. Because of these limitations, the Company uses EBITDA (loss) and Adjusted Gross Margin only in conjunction with GAAP measures of performance, such as net loss and gross margin. In addition, other companies may calculate similarly titled measures differently, so the Company's non-GAAP financial measures may not be comparable to those of other companies.
